title: Coverage viewer, round 2: six ways to fix it
kicker: /babble 6 · 3 on data-ui, 3 hand-rolled · UR5e Entire Workspace, 54 trajectories
brief: Your Nov 24 feedback on the coverage page: headline numbers shown all the time, no drill-in or Rerun from the trajectories table, unexplained row colours, a table that can't filter or save views ("one of our generic tables from data-ui"), and a control strip that shows where it doesn't apply ("a settings gear in the top right"). You asked for 3 proposals built on data-ui and 3 that keep hand-rolling. All six are live prototypes on the same real data, and every one passes your feedback as a pass/fail check.
defaultWhy: V3 · Coverage views in data-ui scores 92/100: the coverage figures become four new data-ui view types (plane, histogram, tool projection, tilt map) inside data-ui's own table, filter, saved views, side panel and gear, with the contract text to land them in data-ui. It is the only direction that scores top marks on both the common visual language and the legends while keeping a full drill with Open in Rerun. Its weak spot is the landing: a wall of number cards, with the tool one tab away.
decisionHinge: How much the common visual language is worth against the landing. Move 10 points from FR5 (data-ui) to FR1 (whole dataset at a glance) and V6 · Who goes there wins 96 to 90: hand-rolled, but its landing shows joints, tool position and pointing on one screen, and clicking any cell lists the trajectories behind it. The splice that keeps both: V3's views and table, with V5's or V6's landing and V6's click-a-cell-to-filter (V2 already shows that click working inside data-ui).
invariants: The same UR5e · Entire Workspace data (54 trajectories, dev + holdout at full speed), from the same traj_compare.coverage payload; the per-trajectory cell lists rebuild the payload's counts exactly (extract.py asserts it).
Same viewport (1440 × 900), same check (check.cjs), same five-step walkthrough shape, all captured from the live prototypes.
Every proposal passes your six feedback points as pass/fail gates before scoring.
boundary: Live prototypes in traj_compare/docs/proposals/coverage-ui-2026-11-24/ on real UR5e data; Open in Rerun really launches Rerun through traj_compare.serve. The pictures here are captures of those prototypes; nothing is wired into traj_compare's real coverage page or into data-ui yet.

variants.name: Stock dashboard
variants.thesis: It really is a dashboard on data: the coverage page built from data-ui exactly as it is today, with zero new data-ui code, plus the honest list of where stock data-ui falls short.
variants.bestWhen: Coverage should be one more data-ui dashboard that an agent edits as YAML (a new figure is a dozen lines of .base, checked by data-ui check), and every future data-ui improvement should land here for free.
variants.losesWhen: A figure needs polish data-ui lacks: no p98-clipped linear scale, the front and side tool views stretch (no equal aspect), titles can't name the picked joint, no highlighting a trajectory across figures, the 3-D voxels ignore the gear.

decisions.label: Figures
decisions.value: Vega-Lite inside .base: rect heatmaps with the limit box, stacked histograms, a polar tilt map, stock voxels.

decisions.label: Gear

decisions.label: Drill

keepParts: rows.py: the payload as row tables, nothing recomputed
the stock trajectories table with saved views and folding split groups

fr1.evidence: The Overview is mostly 15 KPI cards (each footed "the producer's number") plus one tool map; joints, tool and pointing each need their own page, and the front/side tool views stretch.

fr2.evidence: Clicking a row opens data-ui's side panel with its numbers, joint angles over time and Open in Rerun; the table stays beside it. It doesn't draw what the trajectory adds.

fr3.evidence: Stock filter rail, text filter, five saved views as tabs plus + Save, groups that fold, one-click sort (step 4).

fr4.evidence: Settings gear top right repaints every heatmap; the joint picker is a filter on One joint only. The 3-D voxels ignore the gear, and the picker shows a stray "Any" option with counts.

fr5.evidence: Zero new data-ui code: stock rail, dashboards, KPI, table, facets, side panel, voxels; the figures are .base Vega-Lite that any data-ui app can use.

fr6.evidence: One legend line per page instead of per figure; histograms keep a split legend; the KPI footers are noise. No colour beside a trajectory.

variants.name: Rows first
variants.thesis: The dataset is a table of trajectories, and coverage is what the rows you've filtered add up to: tick "holdout" in data-ui's filter rail and every map redraws as what those 12 alone cover.
variants.bestWhen: The question is about a slice: what holdout covers that dev doesn't, what you'd lose by dropping a kind, which trajectory is alone in a corner. Clicking a map cell lists the trajectories through it in data-ui's side panel.
variants.losesWhen: You want density over time (a map counts trajectories, so a long dwell counts once) or the motion itself: the spaghetti, envelope, slabs, parallel coordinates, growth curve and 3-D views are gone because none of them recounts from cell lists.

decisions.label: Spine
decisions.value: One stock data-ui table with a stock filter rail; the tabs are data-ui view tabs.

decisions.label: Maps
decisions.value: A registered "occupancy" view counts trajectories per cell over whatever rows data-ui hands it, labelled "subset n of 54".

decisions.label: Honesty check
decisions.value: With nothing filtered, all 22 grids, the 1 283 voxels and 10 headline numbers must equal analyze's at load, or the page logs an error.

decisions.label: Drill

keepParts: the generic occupancy view (rows list their cells; the view counts)
filter rows → every map recounts, labelled as a subset
click a cell → data-ui's side panel lists who goes there
proof: load-time equality with the payload on every grid

variants.name: Coverage views in data-ui
variants.thesis: Move the coverage figures into data-ui as stock view types (plane, histogram, tool projection, tilt map) with a page-wide settings gear, so every dataset page in every app gets them in the common visual language.
variants.bestWhen: Coverage should look and behave like the rest of your apps and be reusable: any app with rows gets these figures, the table, saved views and side panel from data-ui, and PROPOSED-CONTRACT.md is ready for a data-ui lane to land.
variants.losesWhen: You want the whole picture on the landing (it is a wall of KPI cards; the tool is a tab away), or the figures data-ui can't host yet: the 3-D direction sphere, parallel coordinates, the dataset spaghetti and envelope. Changing a setting redraws the page.

decisions.value: coverage-plane, coverage-hist, coverage-projection and coverage-polar, registered as data-ui plugins from v3/views/.

decisions.label: Rows
decisions.value: One row per grid with counts as list cells (one row per cell only for the stock voxels).

decisions.label: Settings

proof: numbers in the stills match data/ (elbow q×qd 49 % visited, 25 % with ≥ 10 samples, 18 % evenness)

variants.name: Tidy
variants.thesis: Keep today's page, which you like for its glance and its tabs, and fix exactly what you flagged, nothing structural.
variants.bestWhen: You want today's page back with its paper cuts gone and nothing to relearn: same tabs, figures, colours and words.
variants.losesWhen: You want the page to be data-ui: the table only looks like data-ui, its filters and saved views are its own code, and the figures still don't talk to the table.

the gear button that shows the current colour map

variants.name: Focus rail
variants.thesis: Keep the whole dataset on screen, and let a trajectory list on the left light up what any trajectory (or a few) contributes, in every figure at once.
variants.bestWhen: The question is about a trajectory or a set: what dev-029 adds, whether holdout covers anything dev doesn't, which trajectory you could drop. Pressing ↓ in the list and watching every map change scans the set one by one.
variants.losesWhen: You only want the dataset picture: the list takes 300 px all the time. With thousands of trajectories it needs virtualising, and selecting many washes out the highlight.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.value: A resizable trajectory list on the left (filter, sort, group with a dot-colour legend, saved-view chips); tabs on the right.

decisions.label: Selection overlay
decisions.value: Selected cells in the colour map, the rest of the dataset in grey, cells only the selection reaches in cyan, plus "adds N cells nobody else visits".

decisions.label: Landing

decisions.label: Drill

the one-screen landing of joints + tool + pointing

variants.name: Who goes there
variants.thesis: The figures are the query: click any coloured cell to list the trajectories that made it, or an empty one to see who comes closest; clicks add up (AND).
variants.bestWhen: You are curating the dataset: who is behind a hot spot, who almost reaches a gap, so which trajectory to extend or which task to add. Click a region, read the list, drill in, open it in Rerun.
variants.losesWhen: You want coverage recounted for a subset (it fades, never recounts); the 2 cm tool pixels are 3–4 px click targets, and there is no 3-D voxel view, parallel coordinates or growth curve.

decisions.label: Query
decisions.value: A sticky "Who goes there" bar of chips in plain words ("visits shoulder_pan q 0–20°, qd 0–15°/s"), ANDed, with "n of 54 trajectories".

decisions.label: Holes
decisions.value: On Tool position, reachable-but-unvisited pixels turn amber; pins mark the three spots farthest from any path, and a click ranks who comes closest.

decisions.label: Who list
decisions.value: A compact list docked beside every figure tab; hovering a row inks its cells in every figure.

decisions.label: Drill
decisions.value: A drawer that keeps the dataset visible: its cells over the faded dataset, its motion, ‹ › through the answer, Open in Rerun.

keepParts: figures that write the query (a view emits {grid, cells, label})
saved views that also keep the figure query
proof: the walkthrough: one q×qd cell → 8 trajectories, AND a front-view pixel → 1
